verdict_text: NO: the checks use `assert`, which raises `AssertionError` only when run without `-O`/`PYTHONOPTIMIZE`; if the run.sh or environment strips assertions (e.g. `python -O`), the script would silently write a wrong/incomplete output without failing loudly, violating "Required checks... must fail loudly." Also the check for "no tensor of blocks 12,13,14,15 remains" is not verified directly—only the final renumbered set {0..11} is asserted, so a bug in `renumber` mapping (e.g. collision) could still pass the layers==range(12) check without specifically confirming old indices 12-15 are absent as distinct old-key checks, though this is implicitly covered. The main violation is reliance on bare `assert` for the required fail-loud checks, which is fragile and not guaranteed under `-O`.
